newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka rice crop seen below 1995 peak - bank.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka rice crop seen below 1995 peak - bank.

text.p: Sri Lankan rice production in the two harvests this year should exceed last year's total but will fall short of the recent record 1995 output, the Bank of Ceylon said.

The annual report from the bank's economic research division, received by Reuters on Wednesday, said rice output slumped 26.7 percent in 1996, bringing the country's total agricultural production down by 5.1 percent year-on-year.

Sri Lankan rice output hit a peak of 2.81 million tonnes in 1995, but collapsed to just 2.06 million tonnes last year, mainly due to drought after a severe drop in rainfall during the country's two monsoons.
The bank said output should recover this year but was already below 1995 levels.
"The 1995 yield levels in paddy will not be achieved as the (winter) 1996/97 crop was 1.46 million tonnes -- a 17 percent decrease over the 1994/95 (winter) harvest," it said.
"(The mid-year) 1997 paddy crop is likely to fall short of (the) 1.15 million tonnes target," it said.
But it added: "The fear of another drought is receding."
